harness.system_prompt:
You are helm, an agent at the conn of the JobyCorp fleet. Be direct and concise.

Working method: survey before you read. `tree` shows where the mass is, `outline` gives a file's skeleton, `grep` with `context` replaces a read after every hit, `sgrep` answers structural questions (call sites, shapes), and `read` windows are for judgment, not indexing. Files go through the file tools: `read` not cat/sed, `grep` not grep/rg, `glob` not find, `edit`/`write` not sed or heredocs. Bash runs things: builds, tests, mix tasks. Dev servers and long commands run with `bash(background: true)`; `job` polls and kills them. Never signal a process you did not start. Commands must not wait on stdin: pass scripts with `-e` or a file, never an interactive `iex`. Read enough to act, act, verify, and stop.
harness.nudge: Continue until every requirement in the task is done, then reply with the one-line summary.
harness.nudge_policy: once, only after a narrated or blank ending; otherwise abandoned
harness.last_call: Round cap reached — this is the last call. Stop anything you started (background jobs, servers), then reply with the one-line summary: what is done and what is not. No further work.
harness.brief:
# JobyCorp website — design brief

JobyKit is already installed and `benchapp` is a generated JobyKit app that
compiles, boots, and passes its tests. Work inside `benchapp`. Follow the
guidelines in `benchapp/AGENTS.md` and the design direction in
`benchapp/DESIGN.md`; where `DESIGN.md` and this brief differ, this brief
wins.

## The client

JobyCorp is a local AI research company. It runs analysis and benchmarks of
local LLMs on its own hardware and shares the research openly with the
community. The site is JobyCorp's public home: it should tell a visitor
what JobyCorp does, show that the work is real and rigorous, and invite
them to read and follow it.

Use only the facts above. Do not invent statistics, customer names, team
members, awards, dates, or product names. Where a section wants a number
or a name you have not been given, write copy that does not need one.

## Scope

This is a design task. Build the visual identity, the layout, the copy, and
the components. Do not add application features: no forms that submit, no
live data, no countdowns. Static content and navigation only. The app's
databases already exist so the dev server boots; do not add tables,
migrations, schemas, or any use of the Repo — the site has no data.

1. Remove every trace of the generator's demo: the stock `simple_nav`
   header, the "built with" footer, the welcome content of HomeLive, and
   every link to `/design`, `/custom-designs`, and `/design.json`. Those
   pages exist for inspecting the kit and are not part of the product;
   leave their routes in place but nothing on the site may link to or
   mention them.
2. Three pages, all on the same layout: `/` (the landing page),
   `/research` (what JobyCorp publishes and how it tests), and `/about`
   (who JobyCorp is and why the work is shared).
3. A top navigation bar in `Layouts.app` with id `main-nav` that marks the
   current page's link with `aria-current="page"`, collapses behind a
   toggle button with id `nav-toggle` at phone widths, and carries the
   kit's theme toggle with id `theme-toggle`, usable at both widths.
4. A footer that belongs to JobyCorp.
5. The landing page: a hero that says what JobyCorp does in one sentence, a
   section on the research (what is measured and how), a section on the
   hardware and method (local models, local hardware, results published in
   full), and a closing call to action to read the research. Sections are
   yours to add or merge; every section must earn its place.
6. At least one composite component of your own, registered in the
   DesignManifest with a `/design` preview, used on more than one page.

## Design requirements

- Light and dark themes, both finished, with the palette `DESIGN.md`
  defines applied to the `light` and `dark` themes in `app.css` (keep
  those two names; the theme toggle switches by them). Phone and desktop,
  both finished. No horizontal overflow at 390 px. Body text contrast at
  least 4.5:1 and large text at least 3:1 in both themes.
- Every icon name you use must exist in the installed heroicon set; check
  before you use it. A blank icon is a defect.
- Copy is concise: headings of a few words, sentences a visitor can read
  at a glance. Copy is about JobyCorp and its research, never about the
  component kit, the framework, or this task.
- Compose the kit's registered wrappers; raw HTML primitives are a lint
  failure. Lint must be clean.

## Tests

7. Existing tests must pass; update any test that referred to removed
   demo content. No new features. Add a render test for each new page.

## Constraints

- The dev server must run on port 4099; `PORT` is already set. Do not use
  any other port. Do not stop or kill processes you did not start.
- When `mix precommit` and `mix joby_kit.lint` both pass, reply with a
  one-line summary. Do not re-verify: green precommit and clean lint are the
  finish line.

Rebuilt JobyCorp's public site in `benchapp`: replaced the generator demo with a JobyCorp header `#main-nav` (current-page `aria-current`, collapsible `#nav-toggle` at phone, kit theme toggle usable at both widths) and JobyCorp footer, added `/`, `/research`, `/about` on the shared layout — hero with a monospace "run record" composite card (registered in the DesignManifest with a preview, used on home + research), measured-quantity tables, numbered method, and closing research CTA — applied the DESIGN.md signal-teal palette to the `light`/`dark` themes (plotting-paper + figure-table CSS), and added a render test per page; routes for `/design`, `/custom-designs`, `/design.json` remain but nothing links to them.

desktop.text:
JobyCorp
Home
Research
About
Local models, measured and shared

JobyCorp is a local AI research company. It runs analysis and benchmarks of local language models on its own hardware, and shares the research openly with the community.

Why the work is shared

A benchmark only means something if it can be checked. JobyCorp runs the models on machines it owns, under conditions it records, and publishes the results in full — so anyone can see what was measured and repeat it.

Open research is the point of the work. Numbers that sit behind a headline are not the work; the record behind them is.

publish

What a published result includes

Publishing a result means publishing the record: the model, the hardware, the settings, the data, and the numbers that came out of it.

Nothing about how it was got stays private.

part	what it records
model	which weights were measured
hardware	the machine that ran it
settings	how each run was configured
data	what the model was measured on
results	every number, with its unit

JobyCorp
Home
Research
About
JobyCorp measures local language models on its own hardware and publishes every result in full.

We run open models on the machines we own, hold the conditions steady, and share every run — the settings, the data, and the numbers — so anyone can repeat it.

Read the research

identifier
weights
bits
context
tokens
throughput
tok/s

GB
The same fields on every run, so runs compare.

research

What a run measures

Every run is measured against the same fixed set of quantities, on the same hardware, with the settings recorded before anything starts. A number from one model reads against a number from the next.

The fields are few and fixed. Each result reports them with their units — and nothing else.

model	identifier
weights	bits
context	tokens
throughput	tok/s

hardware

publication

desktop.text:
JobyCorp
Home
Research
About
What we publish and how we test

JobyCorp benchmarks local language models on its own hardware. Every result is published with the conditions it was measured under, so it can be read, checked, and repeated.

research

What a run measures

A small, fixed set of quantities. The same fields, the same units, on every run — so a result is a number you can compare, not a paragraph.

Measured on the hardware that ran the model, never carried over from a vendor's spec sheet.

quantity	unit
model	identifier
weights	bits
context	tokens
throughput	tok/s
latency	ms
memory	GB

method

How a run is tested
01
fix the conditions
Choose a model, a machine, and a record of every setting before anything runs.
02
run the workload
The same set of prompts and tasks against each model, so runs differ only in the model.
03
measure the run
Throughput, latency, memory, and tokens, taken under the same conditions and in the same units.
04
publish the record
The method, the hardware, the data, and the numbers — in full.

record

What a record carries

Each run leaves a record with the fields it was measured against. Publishing means publishing that record — the model, the hardware, the settings, and the data — not just the headline number.

A record is the unit of work. Where a section asks for a result, the record tells you how it was got.

run record

model
identifier
weights
bits
context
tokens
throughput
tok/s
latency
ms
memory
GB
Enough to repeat the run, not just admire it.

About

Runs local language models on its own hardware and publishes the results in full.
